solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Got made well again by non-amateur

parts.note: a non-amateur is a professional, a PRO
made well again means cured

explanation.surface: Someone recovered from illness thanks to a professional doctor rather than an amateur healer.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade reads in clue order after the definition 'Got'; 'by' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: To procure something is to obtain it, so procured is a synonym of got in the past tense.

clue.text: Female bird always soaring round middle of lea

indicators.note: round means the reversed word for always goes around the central letter
soaring in a down clue means the word for always reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: ever means always

indicators.note: middle of picks out the central letter of the word lea

explanation.surface: A hen bird rising high, circling above the middle of a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soaring' turns EVER into REVE in this down entry, and 'round' puts it around E.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve is the female of the ruff, a wading bird.

clue.text: Agreed to cooperate, keeping puss inside — not that easy?

indicators.note: keeping means the word for agreed holds another word
inside places the feline word within the first word

parts.note: to comply is to agree to cooperate, so complied
puss is a familiar name for a cat

explanation.surface: Someone agreed to help, keeping the cat indoors, which wasn't simple.
explanation.definitionFit: Complicated means involved and difficult, so not that easy describes it.

clue.text: Cut in money to be paid had to be acknowledged

indicators.note: Cut means the word for money paid to a landlord is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: rent is money to be paid for a property
owned means possessed, had

explanation.surface: A reduction in money owed had to be recognised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' docks the T from RENT; 'in' and 'to be' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Renowned means widely recognised and celebrated, so acknowledged in the sense of famous.

clue.text: Something poisonous — oily danger gents dispersed

indicators.note: dispersed means the letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that a slippery toxic hazard sent the men scattering.
explanation.definitionFit: The destroying angel is a deadly poisonous white Amanita mushroom.

clue.text: Dad handles fruit

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father, Dad
to paw something is to handle it clumsily, so handles gives PAWS

explanation.surface: Father picking up and feeling the fruit at a market stall.
explanation.definitionFit: The papaw (pawpaw) is a tropical fruit, the papaya, so this plural is an example of fruit.

clue.text: Prisoner, sick inside, getting support

indicators.note: inside means the word for unwell sits within the captive's abbreviation

parts.note: POW is a prisoner of war
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A captive who has fallen ill being given some support.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillow supports the head in bed, so it is a kind of support.

clue.text: Illustration put up in municipality

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the letters read upwards, backwards
in means the letters are found within the word municipality

explanation.surface: A picture being displayed in the town hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to CIP inside municipality, and 'put up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pic is short for picture, an illustration.

clue.text: Cascade after breaking into barrier

indicators.note: into means the jumbled letters go inside the word for barrier

parts.note: a wall is a barrier

indicators.note: breaking means the letters of after are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Water tumbling down after bursting through a dam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like a time word placing one thing later, but it is the fodder that 'breaking' scrambles; 'into' then signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterfall is a cascade of water falling over a drop.

clue.text: Sailors from Dover region having the last word

parts.note: Dover is in the south-east of England, abbreviated SE
amen is the word that closes a prayer, the last word

explanation.surface: Mariners from the Kent coast who always insist on finishing the argument.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover is a port in Kent, in the south-east (SE) of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamen are sailors, men who work at sea; a straightforward plural synonym.

clue.text: Lewdness unfortunately returning to conurbation

indicators.note: returning means the interjection for unfortunately is read backwards

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately
a conurbation is a large urban area, a city

explanation.surface: A lament that indecency is sadly coming back to the big city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns ALAS into SALA, which is then followed by CITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Salacity is lustfulness or indecency, so it is a synonym of lewdness.

clue.text: Small room to dispose of commercially, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for selling is heard spoken and a same-sounding word is entered

parts.note: to dispose of goods commercially is to sell them

explanation.surface: A small room being put on the market by an estate agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A cell is a small room, as in a monk's or prisoner's cell.

clue.text: Aggressive types in row at odds with Germans

indicators.note: at odds suggests the letters are in disagreement and so set out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Belligerent people caught up in a quarrel with Germans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at odds' rearranges ROW and GERMANS together; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmongers are people who stir up war, so they are aggressive types.

clue.text: Gale blowing round railway establishment in waiting period

indicators.note: round means the jumbled storm word goes around the railway word
blowing suggests the letters are blown about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a station is a railway establishment

explanation.surface: A storm blowing around a railway station while passengers wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing' signals the anagram and 'round' the containment; the definition is adjectival, so 'in waiting period' describes rather than names.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestational relates to gestation, the period of pregnancy spent waiting for birth.

clue.text: Cold plant location providing stuff for meal

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a rockery is a garden feature where plants are grown among stones

explanation.surface: A chilly spot in the garden that somehow supplies what's needed for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: A rockery is a garden bed of stones and alpine plants, common in British gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Crockery is plates, cups and dishes, the stuff a meal is served on.

clue.text: Teacher smart, doing away with initial chattering

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish teacher of the law

indicators.note: doing away with initial means the first letter of the word for smart is dropped

parts.note: to smart is to sting

explanation.surface: A sharp teacher who gives up opening remarks and starts gossiping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing away with initial' cuts STING to TING. In British English to rabbit on is to chatter at length.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbiting is British slang for talking at length about trivia, chattering.

clue.text: Cleaner sort of drama?

definitions.meaning: a ... opera is a kind of long-running serial drama

explanation.definitionFit: Soap is both a cleaning agent and short for soap opera, a type of television drama.

clue.text: Business not going well — compromise?

parts.note: trade means business, commerce
something off has gone bad, not going well

explanation.surface: A company struggling and looking for some middle ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade-off is a balance between competing aims, a compromise.

clue.text: An objection from neighbour?

definitions.note: neighbour is used as a verb here, to lie next to

parts.note: an gives the indefinite article A
'but' introduces an objection, as in 'no buts'

explanation.surface: A complaint coming from the people next door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neighbour' reads as a noun but must be taken as a verb; the question mark flags that stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to border on or lie adjacent to, which is what to neighbour something means.

clue.text: No jolly fighters needing friendly help in the usual way of things

definitions.text: in the usual way of things

parts.note: taken as written
a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
an ally is a friend who gives help

explanation.surface: Fighting men who are anything but cheerful, relying on support from friends, as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' is not cheerful here: it is naval slang for a Royal Marine, so 'jolly fighters' gives RM.
explanation.definitionFit: Normally means ordinarily, as things usually happen, matching the phrase in the usual way of things.

clue.text: Old boy given 'eave up — one going from bar to bar?

definitions.text: one going from bar to bar?

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a heave up is a hoist; with the dropped H of Cockney speech, as in ''eave', it is 'oist

explanation.surface: An old pal being heaved up after crawling from pub to pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''eave' tells you an H is dropped, so HOIST loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboist plays music, which is written in bars, so the player moves from one bar to the next, not between pubs.

clue.text: Bird handler endlessly excited Pope

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endlessly means the word handler loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A falconer who has been worked up into a frenzy about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts HANDLER to HANDLE; 'excited' then rearranges BIRD and HANDLE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Hildebrand was the given name of Pope Gregory VII, the eleventh-century reforming pontiff.

clue.text: This writer's joining holy warriors

parts.note: the setter referring to themself: this writer is = I'M
pi is informal for pious, holy

explanation.surface: The writer announcing that they are signing up with a band of religious fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer's' is the setter's I'M, the apostrophe-S being 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a Zulu regiment, a body of warriors.

clue.text: Plate is plain, slightly chipped

indicators.note: slightly chipped means the word for plain has a little bit knocked off its end

parts.note: patent means obvious, plain

explanation.surface: A dinner plate described as plain and a little chipped.
explanation.definitionFit: A paten is the plate used for the bread at the Eucharist.

clue.text: King that is wanting alcoholic drink, a type of wine

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
a sling is a mixed drink of spirit, sugar and water, as in a gin sling

explanation.surface: A king without his cocktail having to make do with a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' looks like a deletion signal, but here it simply means needing and links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a white grape and the wine made from it, so it is a type of wine.

clue.text: Music request, the first to be put down

indicators.text: the first to be put down
indicators.note: the first to be put down means the opening letter of the request word moves to the bottom of this down entry

parts.note: to ask is to request

explanation.surface: A musical request at a party, the first record to put on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put down' in a down entry moves the A from the top to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Ska is a Jamaican popular music style, a precursor of reggae.

clue.text: Talk about knight being decorated!

indicators.note: about means the speech word goes around the chess letter

parts.note: to orate is to talk pompously, make a speech
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A speech about a knight who has just been honoured.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a knight being given an honour; 'decorated' is really the adjective for ornamented.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately ornamented, which is what decorated means as an adjective.

clue.text: Startled ruler meeting saint

parts.note: an agha (aga) is an Ottoman commander or chief, a ruler

explanation.surface: A potentate taken by surprise when he meets a holy figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with shock or horror, so it is a near-synonym of startled.

clue.text: Policy by US magazine — a help for survival

parts.note: Life was a famous American photo magazine
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: An insurance policy sold alongside an American magazine as a safety net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Policy' tempts as life insurance, but it gives LINE; 'by' places it beside LIFE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifeline is a rope thrown to save someone, figuratively anything that helps one survive.
